item.title: Arabica Coffee Prices Hit Record on U.S., Colombia Tariff Spat
item.description: Arabica coffee prices hit a record level, as traders digested the withdrawal of President Trump’s threats to impose tariffs and economic sanctions on Colombia.

item.title: Financial Services Roundup: Market Talk
item.description: Gain insight on Experian, SoFi Technologies and more in the latest Market Talks covering Financial Services.

item.title: DeepSeek Won't Sink U.S. AI Titans
item.description: Panic fueling the selloff of Nvidia, Broadcom and other tech giants is overblown.

item.title: Comex Gold, Silver Settle Lower
item.description: Gold settled 1.4% lower, down two of the past three sessions, and silver fell 2.5%, down three of the past four sessions.

item.title: Stocks Sink in Broad AI Rout Sparked by China's DeepSeek
item.description: U.S. stocks were mostly lower, with the Nasdaq leading declines as makers of AI infrastructure suffered steep falls, many in the double digits. Nvidia was down 16%.

item.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
item.description: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

item.title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.description: Longshot is trying to build a gun big enough to make space data centers a reality.

item.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
item.description: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

item.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
item.description: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

item.title: Rivian’s startup Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field
item.description: Field also worked on Apple's secretive car project and oversaw development of the Tesla Model 3.

item.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech’s most expensive mistakes
item.description: The San Francisco startup aims to help battery and chip manufacturers identify defects on production lines, reducing downtime and costly mistakes.

item.title: Licube wants to be the fuel provider to the fusion power industry — see how at TechCrunch Disrupt
item.description: Fusion power plants will need a lot of lithium, and Licube is preparing to be a key supplier.

item.title: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device
item.description: Fusion power startup Cambridge Heavy Industries is building a small, laser-powered fusion device to fuel the coming wave of fusion power plants.

item.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
item.description: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

item.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
item.description: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."

item.title: Helix Carbon says it can make iron cheaper by recycling blast furnace pollution
item.description: The steel industry is a big polluter, but Helix Carbon can upcycle pollution from blast furnaces to drive down emissions and improve margins.

item.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.

item.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
item.description: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

item.title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

item.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
item.description: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
